sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and thorax red-brown, venter and legs paler; antennae and labrum pale yellow; clypeus white; wings grey-yellow, opaque; veins of the marginal field red-yellow. Length with wings 24—26 mm, length without wings 11—13 mm, wingspan about 42 mm. Head large, round, slightly narrowed near the compound eyes; coronal suture distinct, without a transverse groove in front of it, but the area between the compound eyes with irregular shallow wrinkles; length to mandible base 2.37—2.54 mm, maximum width 2.8—3.07 mm. Compound eyes black, well developed, anterior margin straight, posterior margin rounded, maximum diameter 0.47—0.59 mm. Ocelli as circular, fairly large yellow spots, distinctly raised above the head surface (interpreted by Weidner as "antennal spots"). Antennae slender, shorter than the head, 24—27-segmented, mostly 25-segmented; segment 1 longest, segment 2 as long as wide, segment 3 smallest and ring-like (but in the 26-segmented antenna segment 3 is longer than segment 4). Labrum rounded, almost circular. Pronotum narrower than the head (width 2.05—2.33 mm), about 2 times as wide as long; the strongly convex anterior margin of the curved anterior half; sides narrowing posteriorly; posterior margin with a distinct median notch. Legs without lateral spines. Wings long and narrow, reticulate. Forewing 20—23 mm long, 4.2—4.8 mm wide, Sc short; R reaching the middle of C and giving off more than 2 branches; Rs with 5 branches to C and 3 to M; M with 2 main branches; Cu with 9 branches; anal absent. Hindwing almost as forewing, with a weak anal. Abdomen oval, slightly wider than the thorax. Cerci small, conical. Styli very small, smaller than the cerci, present in both sexes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head red-brown, smooth, with a few hairs; mandibles black; antennae, labrum and pronotum red-yellow; remainder yellow-white. Total length including mandibles about 14 mm, size very variable. Head subrectangular, posterior margin rounded (length including mandibles 4.6—6.5 mm, length to mandible base 2.44—2.91 mm, maximum width 2.50—3.78 mm); coronal suture distinct. Compound eyes black, distinct but smaller than in the alate; anterior margin nearly straight; about 2 times as long as wide. Ocelli small and round, raised above the head surface (interpreted by Weidner as "antennal spots"). Mandibles large, straight but incurved and pointed near the apex (left mandible 2.5 mm long); each with 2 large, pointed marginal teeth. Labrum large, subrectangular, narrowing posteriorly. Clypeus band-like. Antennae slender, shorter than the head; number of segments unknown (the antenna figured by Weidner is broken, with 22 segments). Postmentum band-like, sides nearly parallel, only very weakly incurved (unlike A. macrocephalus and others). Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, weakly saddle-shaped (anterior end upturned); anterior margin strongly convex, without a median notch; posterior margin without a median notch. Abdomen semitransparent, gut contents visible.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head orange; remainder pale red-yellow; compound eyes and mandibles darker. Total length 6—10 mm. Head round, almost oval. Compound eyes dark brown. Ocelli small, as dark spots. Antennae 24—25-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped, divided into two halves by a transverse groove. Cerci present; styli short and pointed.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Roonwal & Bose (1988), original in English; that work states its description follows Hagen (1858) and Weidner (1960); the alate, soldier and worker sections are all present; figure numbers (Fig. 21—23), measurement tables (Table 1—2) and type and locality records are not translated; the number of antennal segments in the soldier is missing in the original (only Weidner's figure of a broken 22-segmented antenna is recorded); one character of OCR residue remains at the wingspan, recorded here as 42 mm.
